title: The Churning of the Ocean
text:
In Hindu tradition, the gods, the devas, had lost their strength and were losing their long war against their rivals, the asuras. The god Vishnu told them that they could regain their power by drinking amrita, the nectar of immortality, which lay hidden at the bottom of the cosmic ocean of milk. But the ocean had to be churned to bring it up, and that task was too great for the gods alone. They would have to work with their enemies.

So devas and asuras made a truce. They uprooted Mount Mandara to use as a churning rod and wrapped the great serpent Vasuki around it as a rope. The asuras held one end and the devas the other, and they pulled back and forth. When the mountain began to sink into the ocean, Vishnu took the form of a giant tortoise and held it up on his back.

The churning brought up wonders, and also a deadly poison that threatened to destroy the world. Shiva drank it and held it in his throat, which turned blue. At last the physician of the gods rose with the pot of amrita. The asuras seized it, but Vishnu, disguised as the enchanting Mohini, distracted them and served the nectar to the devas.
lesson: Some goals are too large for any one side, and reaching them may require working with people you distrust. Agree in advance how the results will be shared, or the cooperation will end in a fight.
people: The devas, the asuras, Vishnu, Shiva, the serpent Vasuki
source: Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Astika Parva); Bhagavata Purana, Book 8; Vishnu Purana
